newsitem.title: CHINA: China says human rights could complicate U.S. ties.
newsitem.headline: China says human rights could complicate U.S. ties.

text.p: China said on Thursday that slowly warming Sino-U.S. ties could be complicated if the United States decided to confront Beijing on the issue of human rights.

"If the human rights question is made into an issue to interfere in China's internal affairs, then this problem will become more and more complicated," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a regular news briefing.
"The Chinese government cannot accept... using the human rights question to put pressure on the Chinese government or to interfere in China's internal affairs," Shen said.

He was asked for China's response after U.S. Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright said at her Senate confirmation hearing on Wednesday that the United States could co-sponsor a resolution criticising China's human rights record.
The resolution might be presented before the United Nations Human Rights Commission when it meets in Geneva early this year.
Differences in the views of China and the United States towards human rights were normal and could be resolved through talks, Shen said.
"But if you are confrontational then the basis for dialogue will be lost," Shen said.
Albright said Washington's focus towards Beijing would be on "Chinese integration, not isolation".
Sino-U.S. relations have been repeatedly marred by wrangling over human rights.
Washington has slammed Beijing for jailing political dissidents and for its heavy-handed rule in Tibet.
Beijing defends its human rights record by pointing to rising living standards and booming economic growth.
